claims.claim: PHE identified 15,841 positive results not included in reported daily cases, dated 25 September to 2 October
claims.passage: 15,841 cases between 25 September and 2 October were not included
claims.notes: Matches the PHE statement as fetched (WebFetch summary quoting the statement).

claims.claim: 11,968, over 75%, should have been reported between 30 September and 2 October
claims.passage: Of these, over 75% (11,968) relate to cases that should have been reported between 30 September and 2 October.
claims.notes: Verbatim in PHE statement.

claims.claim: Overnight on Friday 2 October 2020 PHE identified the issue
claims.passage: A technical issue was identified overnight on Friday 2 October in the data load process
claims.notes: Also in DHSC weekly statistics: 'A technical issue was identified overnight on Friday 2 October'.

claims.claim: Everyone affected "received their COVID-19 test result as normal."
claims.passage: Every one of these cases received their COVID-19 test result as normal
claims.notes: Quoted fragment is verbatim.

claims.claim: All outstanding cases transferred to contact tracing "by 1am on 3 October."
claims.passage: Outstanding cases reached the contact tracing system by 1am on 3 October.
claims.notes: Wording confirmed via WebFetch summary; same phrase 'by 1am on 3 October' appears verbatim in the Harding reply extract.

claims.claim: "some files containing positive test results exceeded the maximum file size."
claims.passage: some files containing positive test results exceeded the maximum file size
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: "data load process that transfers COVID-19 positive lab results into reporting dashboards"
claims.passage: The issue occurred in the "data load process that transfers COVID-19 positive lab results into reporting dashboards,"
claims.notes: Confirmed in first fetch; second fetch only returned the opening words 'data load process', so full phrase rests on one fetch.

claims.claim: The PHE statement does not use the words Excel, XLS, rows or columns
claims.passage: Excel/XLS/rows/columns: None of these terms appear on the page.
claims.notes: Absence claim confirmed by fetch summary (not a full-text search of the raw page).

claims.claim: Michael Brodie, Interim Chief Executive; published 4 Oct 2020, updated 5 Oct 2020; mitigation "splits large files"
claims.passage: A rapid mitigation has been put in place that splits large files
claims.notes: Dates and title also confirmed by fetch.

claims.claim: Hansard vol 681, 5 October 2020, Covid-19 Update
claims.passage: Covid-19 Update Volume 681: debated on Monday 5 October 2020
claims.notes: Header of the local extract; extract runs complete to the end of the debate.

claims.claim: 15,841 over the previous 8 days; "a failure in the automated transfer of files"
claims.passage: Public Health England identified that over the previous eight days, 15,841 positive test results were not included in the reported daily cases. This was due to a failure in the automated transfer of files from the labs to PHE’s data systems.
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: the problem "emerged in a PHE legacy system"; decided in July to replace; contracts "awarded in August"
claims.passage: The problem emerged in a PHE legacy system. We had already decided in July to replace this system, and I commissioned a new data system to replace the legacy one. Contracts were awarded in August
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: "a maximum file size error"
claims.passage: However, the challenge of a maximum file size error is that it would not necessarily have appeared on that sort of flow chart
claims.notes: Said by the Health Secretary in reply to Alison McGovern.

claims.claim: 6,500 hours of extra contact tracing; "51% of the cases have now been contacted a second time for contact tracing purposes" as of 9am
claims.passage: We brought in 6,500 hours of extra contact tracing over the weekend. I can report to the House that, as of 9 am today, 51% of the cases have now been contacted a second time for contact tracing purposes.
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: "This incident should never have happened"
claims.passage: This incident should never have happened, but the team have acted swiftly to minimise its impact.
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: In Hansard the word Excel appears only in questions from 2 opposition MPs (Ashworth, Coyle); Health Secretary said it 0 times
claims.passage: Why are critical databases in a national pandemic being hosted on Excel spreadsheets? ... why no other Government in the world have experienced such problems with Excel spreadsheets
claims.notes: Grep of the whole extract finds 'Excel' only in Ashworth (2x, Lab/Co-op, Leicester South) and Coyle (1x, Bermondsey and Old Southwark, Lab) plus 'Excellence' in a Hancock answer; none in any Hancock answer.

claims.claim: Quoted question: "Why are critical databases in a national pandemic being hosted on Excel spreadsheets?"
claims.passage: Why are critical databases in a national pandemic being hosted on Excel spreadsheets? Why are they not using specialist database software?
claims.notes: Said by Jonathan Ashworth.

claims.claim: Clark letter 8 Oct: Secretary of State told the House the issue "was related to a Public Health England (PHE) legacy system, which included the use of Microsoft Excel."
claims.passage: The Secretary of State for Health and Social Care told the House on Monday 5 October that the issue was related to a Public Health England (PHE) legacy system, which included the use of Microsoft Excel.
claims.notes: Verbatim. Hansard shows the Secretary of State did not say this; exhibit reports it as the letter's statement.

claims.claim: "It is reported that PHE developers used an old format of the software, XLS, which had a set number of rows to log data that was incompatible with the volume of data being generated."
claims.passage: It is reported that PHE developers used an old format of the software, XLS, which had a set number of rows to log data that was incompatible with the volume of data being generated.
claims.notes: Verbatim; exhibit correctly treats it as unverified reporting.

claims.claim: Greg Clark is Chair of the Science and Technology Committee; letter dated 8 October 2020; question on "the Microsoft Excel-based system"
claims.passage: From Rt Hon Greg Clark MP, Chair 8 October 2020 ... What certification took place of the Microsoft Excel-based system
claims.notes: Committee name comes from Harding reply letterhead (SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY SELECT COMMITTEE).

claims.claim: Harding 12 Oct: "The technical issue was not caused by the use of an old format."
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: The technical issue was not caused by the use of an old format.
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: Increased Pillar 2 volumes "meant that some Excel files used in the transfer process exceeded their file size threshold and so were not uploaded."
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: Increased testing volumes from Pillar 2 meant that some Excel files used in the transfer process exceeded their file size threshold and so were not uploaded.
claims.notes: Body words 'increased Pillar 2 testing volumes' are a paraphrase outside quote marks; quoted portion verbatim.

claims.claim: Reply dates cases 24 September to 1 October, 1 day earlier than PHE
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: The delayed reports are all positive cases identified via Pillar 2 testing between 24 September and 1 October.
claims.notes: PHE 25 Sep to 2 Oct; offset is 1 day at each end, arithmetic holds.

claims.claim: Reply: 6,000 hours of extra contact tracing; "(75% / 11,968)"
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: the vast majority (75% / 11,968) related to cases that should have been reported between30 September and 2 October ... we brought in 6,000 hours of extra contact tracing
claims.notes: Verbatim, including the 6,000 vs Hansard 6,500 discrepancy.

claims.claim: "As of the morning of 12 October, 79% of people testing positive have been reached and asked for details of their contacts."
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: As of the morning of 12 October, 79% of people testing positive have been reached and asked for details of their contacts.
claims.notes: Verbatim; exhibit says it does not assume the figure refers only to the 15,841, which is the correct reading of the letter.

claims.claim: "A full wash-up of the incident is ongoing" (12 Oct); none found published
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: A full wash-up of the incident is ongoing.
claims.notes: Quote verbatim; 'none found published' is a labeled absence claim by the site, not a sourced fact. Verdict row says the reply 'promised' a wash-up, a stronger word than 'is ongoing'.

claims.claim: DHSC weekly statistics (updated 22 Oct 2020): 15,841 cases identified between 25 September and 2 October
claims.source: Department of Health and Social Care
claims.passage: After rapid investigation, 15,841 cases were identified between 25 September and 2 October ... that were not included in the reported daily COVID-19 cases ... Updated 22 October 2020
claims.notes: Confirmed by fetch.

claims.claim: OSR blog 15 Oct 2020: the error "was not directly part of official statistics production"
claims.passage: While the error with the Excel spreadsheet was not directly part of official statistics production
claims.notes: Fetch returned the clause in quotation; date 15 October 2020 confirmed.

claims.claim: OSR launched a review of reproducible analytical pipelines
claims.passage: This is why at OSR we have launched a review to explore the use of RAP across government statistics in more detail.
claims.notes: 'launched' is the OSR's own word.

claims.claim: Archive: figures by publish date "may include the publication of a backlog of data."
claims.passage: Data presented by ‘publish date’ is not a reliable indicator of trends over time since this represents the date on which data was first published and may include the publication of a backlog of data or subsequent revisions to the data.
claims.notes: Body quote is a verbatim fragment but stops mid-clause and puts the period inside the quote; the source continues 'or subsequent revisions to the data'. The sources-list text also closes the quote at 'data' with no ellipsis. Truncation does not reverse the meaning.

claims.claim: "It has not been possible to fully validate these archived datasets against the latest version of the decommissioned Coronavirus (COVID-19) in the UK dashboard."
claims.passage: It has not been possible to fully validate these archived datasets against the latest version of the decommissioned Coronavirus (COVID-19) in the UK dashboard.
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: Archive page last updated 1 May 2025
claims.passage: Last updated on Thursday, 1 May 2025 at 02:43pm
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.notes: The archive page gives no file dates and I could not read file timestamps with the tools available; this date is unverified by me and the caller must confirm it from the zip listing or cut it.

claims.claim: Narrator never accuses a person or country; Clark, Harding, Hancock, Ashworth, Coyle named
claims.notes: Every named person is tied to a Hansard or committee-letter paper trail and reported speech; 'Who lied: Nobody, on the record' is an institutional framing; no accusation found.

claims.claim: verdictNote: "The explanation most people remember, an old spreadsheet running out of rows"
claims.notes: No listed source says what most people remember; the letter only supports that the row-limit story entered the record after 'It is reported'.

claims.claim: Verdict row: 'no document disputes it' (the 15,841)
claims.notes: No listed document disputes the figure, but the Harding reply never states it, so 'no document disputes it' is an absence claim over the listed sources only.
